problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
${x}^{2}-5{y}^{2}+2x+10y=9?$

feedback.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$3{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}-12x+24y=36?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}-12x+24y & =36 \\ 3{x}^{2}-12x-4{y}^{2}+24y & =36 \\ 3[{x}^{2}-4x]-4[{y}^{2}-6y] & =36 \\ 3[(x-2)^{2}-4]-4[(y-3)^{2}-9] & =36 \\ 3(x-2)^{2}-12-4(y-3)^{2}+36 & =36 \\ 3(x-2)^{2}-4(y-3)^{2} & =12 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{3} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the center is $(2,3).$
